clue.text: One supposedly cool copper to get in the way

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to cumber is an old verb meaning to hamper or obstruct

explanation.surface: A police officer who keeps calm is about to obstruct someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman in the surface, but here it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial simile 'cool as a ...' names this salad vegetable as the very model of calmness.

clue.text: Oxford location which charmed courts terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these eighteen letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A place in Oxford that won the hearts of judges, to an awful degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'which charmed courts' is the fodder, all eighteen letters, though 'which' looks like a mere link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the riverside meadow beside the Oxford college and cathedral, a famous spot in the city.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
Representative ordered claim be met

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand that has been satisfied, set out in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as 'commanded' alongside 'claim', but it signals the anagram of CLAIM BE MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for or typifies a wider thing, so it is representative of it.

clue.text: Assign to a small volume right to rewrite

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of volume
to edit a text is to rewrite or revise it

explanation.surface: Someone allots a short book the right to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small volume' suggests a slim book, but it is a unit of measure, CC for cubic centimetres.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit or attribute something to someone is to assign it to them.

clue.text: Spirit's getting comedian drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters of the comic are scrambled

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic is getting tipsy on spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit's' looks like a possessive about liquor, but it defines an adjective meaning of or like a spirit; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A daemon is a supernatural being or attendant spirit, so the adjective describes what belongs to such a spirit.

clue.text: Looking after supermodel almost walking slowly

indicators.note: after places the word for looking behind the shortened name
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the model's name is dropped

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous British supermodel
eying means looking at closely

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing a famous model as they stroll lazily past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supermodel' means Kate Moss, a famous British model; the Looking piece is a spelling of eyeing, and it goes in second although it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To mosey is to wander along in a leisurely, unhurried way.

clue.text: Regret doll being misheard with indistinct sound

indicators.note: being misheard means the words are heard as something they are not, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: to rue is to regret, and Barbie is the famous fashion doll

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a misheard toy doll that mumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE BARBIE said quickly sounds like the word built from rhubarb, the murmur actors make for background crowd noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is theatrical crowd murmur, so something with that quality has a muffled, unclear babble.

clue.text: See 5across
Great 'ero in classic but cut up

indicators.note: in means the hero's name is put inside the Latin word

parts.note: sed is Latin, a classical language, for but
Hector was the great Trojan hero; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'ero shows, he becomes Ector

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker's great hero appears in a classic but has been edited down.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ero tells you to drop the H of the hero too; 'classic' means classical, i.e. Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divided into sectors has been cut up into sections.

clue.text: See 5across
Sailor to go off clutching Princess lie can't wait single clues

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so the princess is placed within the verb

parts.note: eggs that go off are said to addle
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A seaman about to turn bad grabs a princess and tells an untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutching' puts the princess just inside the go-off verb. The trailing words 'can't wait single clues' are stray page text in this copy and take no part in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word means a petty falsehood or a fib, a kind of lie.

clue.text: Gay scene's taking notice of Nirvana

indicators.note: taking means the scene's word takes in the notice, holding it inside

parts.note: gay Paree is the stock phrase for Paris, so belonging to that scene is Parisian
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: The gay scene is taking an interest in blissful enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay scene' is Paris, as in the old phrase 'Gay Paree', not a modern nightlife; 'taking' puts the notice inside the adjective after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect bliss, a heaven, so the adjective describes what belongs to paradise.

clue.text: Beaten back left without sign of life

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for left goes round the vital sign

parts.note: Reds are the political left
a pulse is the first sign of life a medic checks for

explanation.surface: Someone driven off was abandoned with no heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old meaning 'outside': the political colour wraps around the sign of life.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to drive it back, so a repelled force has been beaten back.

clue.text: Shattered aluminium dial's tip on balance

parts.note: all in is an idiom for exhausted or shattered
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

indicators.note: the tip of the dial here is its final letter

explanation.surface: An aluminium dial broken at the tip is weighed on scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' looks like broken metal but means worn out, ALL IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means taking everything into account, which is what on balance also says.

clue.text: Passing fads, somehow hep, a mere fancy

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unexplained route, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Short-lived crazes are somehow hip, a mere whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' signals the anagram of HEP A MERE; 'fancy' completes the surface as a nod to the same shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: These are things of fleeting interest or brief life, such as short-lived crazes.

clue.text: Province in Wessex is alight

parts.note: the Earl of Wessex was the title of the late Queen's youngest son
to alight is to come down to earth after a flight

explanation.surface: A province in the old West Country kingdom is on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wessex' is not the region but the earldom, held by the late Queen's youngest son; 'alight' means come down, not burning.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of Canada's provinces, the smallest, an island in the Gulf of St Lawrence.

clue.text: See 19
See 19
Money donated illustrates changing

indicators.note: changing means altering form, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Money given away shows how things alter.
explanation.walkthrough: All eighteen letters of DONATED ILLUSTRATES are the fodder; 'changing' looks like small change but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official currency of America, so it is money.

clue.text: Butterflies landing on fatal day

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage for boats
the Ides of March was the fatal day for Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: Butterflies settling on a doomed day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' suggests a butterfly alighting, but it is a jetty, PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the family of whites and yellows, such as the cabbage white butterfly.

clue.text: See 22across
Sloths, etc, in luxuriant garden vale

parts.note: Eden is the lush garden of Genesis
vale is Latin for farewell, so goodbye, ta-ta

explanation.surface: Sloths and similar creatures live in a lush valley garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vale' looks like a valley but is the Latin farewell, giving TA-TA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the order of toothless mammals including sloths, anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: See 22across
Be bound and executed

parts.note: bound for somewhere means headed there

explanation.surface: Someone tied up and put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests tied up, but it means on the way, as in bound for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's head on the block is a classic form of execution.
